chunks.content: # CLO Tips Mini-Class: Creating Garment Effects from Flat Patterns This document explains the process of creating garment special effects in CLO using flat patterns, UV mapping, OBJ file export/import, morph targets, animation setup, and video export options. Key terminology includes UV editor, OBJ format, morph targets, animation mode, rendering, and video capture. --- ## Preparing Clothing Patterns and UV Mapping in CLO This section covers selecting garment patterns, preparing UV maps, and exporting OBJ files with proper UV coordinates for further use in 3D garment animation and effects. - Open your garment project in CLO. - Select all pattern pieces (versions) to work on. - In the Properties Editor, use the selection tool ("Seal" selection) to ensure correct pattern selection; incorrect selections will cause later conversion failures. - Open the UV Editor to prepare the UV layout of the patterns. - Flatten the pattern pieces by clicking "Rearrange 2D Location" to optimize the UV layout. - You can hide sewing lines to view patterns more clearly. - Adjust the pattern layout as needed for optimal UV mapping. - Export the flattened patterns as an OBJ file: - Select the specific objects (pattern pieces) you want to export. - Choose "Unified UV Coordinates" to maintain consistent UV mapping. - For higher resolution textures, set the image size to 2048 pixels. - Save the OBJ file along with its associated texture file (usually a text or image file). - Additional details on UV processing and 3D file formats were covered in previous tutorials. --- ## Importing Garments and Setting Up Morph Targets in CLO This section describes importing OBJ files into a new CLO project, configuring the object types, and creating morph targets for garment animation. - Open a new project file in CLO. - Import the previously exported OBJ file: - When selecting object type, choose "Avatar" for the base import. - Do not select the other two object options (unspecified). - After importing, switch to high-quality rendering mode to view the garment clearly. - Import the OBJ file again, this time selecting "Morph Target" as the object type: - Morph targets allow the garment to change shape dynamically during animations. --- ## Animation Setup and Preview in CLO This section explains how to access animation mode, preview animations, add keyframes, and control garment rotation for effect visualization. - Switch to Animation Mode in CLO. - You will find existing change animations in the timeline below. - Press "Play" to preview the animation of garment transformation. - Add keyframes to control the rotation angle or other properties of the garment during the animation. - Load additional animations, such as running sequences, to see the garment in motion. - Animations can be recorded with or without a 3D camera, depending on your needs. --- ## Video Export and Background Settings This section details two methods for exporting garment animations as videos and customizing background settings for easier post-production. - **Rendering Export:** - Export the animation through the rendering window.

It emphasizes the importance of proper pattern selection, UV preparation, and animation keyframing to achieve realistic garment transformations in 3D.
